_: The derived Pragmatica version declaration for issue #60, SPLIT INTO TWO FIELDS by the owner's ruling of 2026-09-11. ai-tools/pragmatica-pins.py carries the mechanism and, more importantly, what a green result does NOT mean; read that first. The single `pinned` field it replaces was answering two questions at once — what a reader's build should depend on, and what a human had actually re-read the API against — so it could never move: bumping it re-asserted every verification nobody had performed, and holding it still left every dependency snippet stale. Neither answer was available while one field carried both.

depends_on._: The version a reader's build should use. A dependency coordinate, nothing more. It tracks Maven Central mechanically and needs no human judgement to move: a coordinate is right when it resolves and names what Central last published. Every <version> under an org.pragmatica-lite groupId, every org.pragmatica-lite:<artifact>:<version> coordinate, and every pragmatica*.version property in this repository is compared against it.
depends_on._artifacts: Artifacts in the group this value speaks for. org.pragmatica-lite:jbct-maven-plugin is at 0.4.6 and releases on its own line, so comparing it here would demand a wrong edit forever; it carries not-core inventory entries instead. org.pragmatica-lite:jackson shares the release line and is published at 1.0.0-rc3 (read from its own maven-metadata.xml, 2026-09-11); examples/pom.xml drives it from the same property, which is why moving that property was checked against Central for BOTH artifacts and not just core.
depends_on.why: Central published 1.0.0-rc3 on 2026-09-02 (lastUpdated 20260902212949) and the repository declared 1.0.0-rc1. Under the single-field declaration this bump was blocked, because it would also have moved two chapter headers and two agent descriptions that assert what somebody read. Split apart, the coordinate axis has no such cost and no such judgement: it now agrees with Central.

_pinned: COMPATIBILITY ALIAS, not a third opinion. website/build.js:55 reads `PIN_DECL.pinned` and that file is owned by an open pull request (#75), so the key stays until #75 lands and build.js can read depends_on.version directly. It is NOT trusted: pragmatica-pins.py --check FAILS if it differs from depends_on.version, because two keys holding one value is the same defect this split exists to remove, one level down. The site renders a dependency coordinate, so the alias mirrors depends_on and never verified_against.

verified_against._: The version at which a human actually re-read the API surfaces a document describes. It moves only when a person does that work, and NEVER by sed: advancing the literal without the re-read fabricates a verification. It is NOT one value, and the evidence for that is in the repository rather than in this comment — see `_shape` below.
verified_against._shape: PER SCOPE, where a scope is a documentation surface someone re-reads as a unit. Determined empirically, not assumed: (1) two values coexist TODAY — book/introduction.md:3 and book/from-process-to-patterns.md:3 say 1.0.0-rc1 while book-aether/appendix-a-api-reference.md:4 says 1.0.0-rc3 — so a single global field is already false for one of them; (2) the two are not a disagreement but verifications of DIFFERENT surfaces: the Aether appendix's own text reads 'Every signature below was read from Pragmatica source at release-1.0.0-rc3 head e123caafb (2026-08-26)' and then says the core types 'are the JBCT book's territory and its appendix covers them; this one starts where Aether starts' — it explicitly disclaims covering Pragmatica Core at all; (3) per-BOOK undercounts, because ai-tools/agents/jbct-coder.md:5 and ai-tools/agents/jbct-reviewer.md:11 carry their own 'with Pragmatica Core <version>' claims next to their own independent last-modified dates (2026-09-06 and 2026-04-06), and neither is a book. Three scopes, two distinct values, one of them about a surface that is not Pragmatica Core.
verified_against._why_not_merged: jbct-book and jbct-tooling hold the same value today, so nothing in the current numbers forces them apart. They are kept apart on the repository's own recorded history instead: CLAUDE.md states the skills and agents are DERIVED artifacts that 'have drifted from it before', ai-tools/check-drift.sh exists because of that drift, and the two surfaces carry independent last-modified stamps. Merging them would mean that re-reading the book at a new release either fabricates a verification for a skill nobody touched, or blocks the book's — which is exactly the defect that splitting `pinned` was meant to remove, reproduced one level down. This is a judgement, and it is marked as one.

upstream._: The external fact the old hard-coded constant was never compared against. <release> is what Maven Central last published. Read 2026-09-11: 1.0.0-rc3, lastUpdated 20260902212949 — unchanged since the 2026-09-09 reading. This axis compares Central against depends_on ONLY. It has nothing to say about verified_against, which is a claim about human work and can never be settled by a repository probe: an upstream release does not re-read anything.
upstream._known_behind_removed: The known_behind deferral is DELETED, per the instruction it carried ('Delete this key when the pin moves — with it gone the check fails until declaration and Central agree'). depends_on and Central now both read 1.0.0-rc3, so the axis is green on agreement rather than on an exception, and it goes red the day Central publishes rc4.

known_versions._: Every version org.pragmatica-lite:core has published, read from maven_metadata. It bounds the safety net: an UNATTRIBUTED literal is only worth a human's classification when Pragmatica has really shipped that version. Without it the check demands entries for all 111 book versions, POM model versions and URL fragments in the tree, and an inventory that size gets routed around rather than maintained. Refresh it in the same PR that moves depends_on — note that plain 1.0.0 is NOT yet a published version, so a GA release must add it here.
known_versions._read_at: Re-read in full on 2026-09-11: 38 <version> entries, byte-identical to the 2026-09-09 list. The date moved; the list did not.

space._: Subtracted from `git ls-files`. Every glob here is a dated record whose job is to name old versions. Anything else removed from the search must be argued for in writing, because a narrowed space was defect (b) of the check this replaces.
space._self_exclude: EXACT paths, matched by string equality and never as globs, printed by name on the space line. These two files quote version literals in prose ABOUT pins, which the scan reads back as pins — the instrument seeing itself. Never widen this to `ai-tools/` or any directory: ai-tools/skills/ and ai-tools/agents/ carry real pins and are precisely what defect (b) was about, and a broadened exclusion would still exit 0, so nothing would report the loss.

_field_assignment: Which of the two fields an occurrence belongs to. Two mechanical rules decide the unambiguous forms and are not listed here: a DEPENDENCY COORDINATE (a <version> under an org.pragmatica-lite groupId, a full org.pragmatica-lite:<artifact>:<version>, or a pragmatica*.version property) is depends_on; a PROVENANCE FORM (a literal written as `release-<version>`, or a `**Based on:**` header line) is verified_against. Everything else is DECLARED below, because nothing in the text distinguishes 'the build uses rc1' from 'somebody read rc1' — the same reason the inventory's classes are declared rather than inferred. An attributed, non-excepted occurrence that neither rule nor declaration reaches FAILS as unassigned; it is never defaulted, because defaulting a verification stamp into the coordinate field is exactly how a fabricated verification would get sed'd in.

_render_exceptions: EMPTY, and that is the ruling's visible effect on the site. Read by website/build.js only, which guards website/content/*.md by coordinate form. The single entry here excepted website/content/aether.md for stating 1.0.0-rc3 while the repository declared 1.0.0-rc1. depends_on is now 1.0.0-rc3, so the page's coordinates equal the pin and the build passes on AGREEMENT rather than on a written-down disagreement. The page was deliberately NOT converted to {{PRAGMATICA_VERSION}}: its line also carries the `org.pragmatica-lite.aether:*` wildcard, which is a separate open question (see _open_questions), and templating the core half while the wildcard stayed literal would split one sentence across two mechanisms and let the unverified half drift silently at the next bump.
_open_questions: Carried forward, unresolved, from the inventory entry this ruling retired — recorded here so it does not vanish with the exception that used to hold it. Whether `org.pragmatica-lite.aether:*` in website/content/aether.md:5 is a true wildcard is NOT settled. Two attempts to check it used unsound instruments: probing module names absent at the tag, and an artifactId extraction that disagreed with `git ls-tree`. The version half of that claim is now correct; the artifact half is still unverified, and no check in this repository examines it.
